title: A Multi-level Bias Elimination through a Decoding Approach with Knowledge Augmentation for Robust Constitutional Alignment of Language Models
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measures representational and inferential bias related to religion by calculating the 'Identity Inference Rate' (IIR). This metric quantifies a model's propensity to infer or predict specific religious identities (e.g., Muslim, Hindu, Sikh) when presented with prompts where the identity term has been masked, particularly in stereotypical contexts.
findings: Large Language Models, including state-of-the-art ones like GPT-4o, exhibit significant and salient biases related to religion within the Indian context. They frequently associate specific religious groups with stereotypes, such as linking Muslims with terrorism or Sikhs with separatism, as measured by a high Identity Inference Rate (IIR). The proposed AMBEDKAR framework, an inference-time decoding strategy, achieves a substantial absolute reduction in this bias (up to 26.41%) across various models and languages (English and Hindi) without needing retraining.
